newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thailand allows closed finance firms to complete deals.
newsitem.headline: Thailand allows closed finance firms to complete deals.

text.p: Thailand's Securities Exchange Commision (SEC) said on Monday it had allowed 16 suspended finance companies to engage in limited operations to complete selected transactions in progress.

In a statement, the SEC said the financially distressed firms, which were suspended from operations on Friday for 30 days, were allowed to transfer promissory notes to other company's handling a depositor guarantee scheme.
They were also permitted to complete payment and transactions for securities bought for clients or the firm's own portfolio before their June 27 suspension.
The firms are also allowed to settle payment with investors who have sold shares through the suspended firms, the statement said.
They are permitted to engage in these activities only if clients have no outstanding debts to the firm at the time of the company's closure last week, it added.
The companies can recover and pursue margin loan repayments from investors owing money to the firms for shares bought on the broker's credit, the SEC said.
The firms are able to transfer shares held by investors wishing to sell securities subject to tender offers, the statement said.
Suspended firms may only sell shares in their own portfolios under tender if the offer price is above the share's current market price, the statement said.
Closed firms must explain all cheques issued to the processing bank and all cheque recipients must provide evidence that they received the funds to settle one of the permitted transactions.

The SEC had decided upon these regulations after meeting with the central bank and the Stock Exchange of Thailand, and the Bank Of Thailand will circulate the order to the 16 suspended firms, the SEC said.
The central bank took the unprecedented step of closing 16 financially-distressed firms on Friday as part of its on-going efforts to bolster the stability of the finance sector.
It has given them 14 days to present rescue plans or face being taken over by the central bank and absorbed by financially-sound firms.
Since Friday there has been doubt about which actions the closed firms were permitted to take.
Some promissory note depositors wishing to participate in a creditor protection scheme have complained that some of the 16 firms failed to cooperate in the scheme on Monday.

The Thai finance and securities sector is struggling to cope with declining revenues, high funding costs and a deterioration in asset quality as Thailand goes through its worst economic downturn for more than a decade.
